body.statement: For every feasible treated-count table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary counts and menus constant in \(a\), the equality \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}=R^\star\) holds if and only if the finite system in \(\texttt{def:independence-feasibility-system}\) is feasible. At every feasible solution, all assignment orbits with positive independent-design mass attain the common dual value, and every positive-likelihood observation cell uses the posterior-mean decision specified in \(\texttt{def:dual-game}\); zero-likelihood cells may take any value in \([-L,L]\).
body.justification: This gives an exact, finite answer to when common-probability independent saturation loses nothing.
body.gap: Hull2026 proves independence minimaxity under no interference, while CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 compares saturation dispersion for a difference-in-means estimator under a linear interference model; neither gives an if-and-only-if frontier for unrestricted estimators under exact-count interference.
body.consumer: A trial planner can test whether ordinary independent cluster saturation is certified minimax before adopting a correlated mechanism.
